own_report_full_span.literal:
R4-1913144	TP to TR38.831: On REFSENS for Inter-band CA
					38.831	  CR-  rev  Cat:  (Rel-16) v0.1.0
					Source: Qualcomm Incorporated
We propose refsens requirement for FR2 interband DL CA

Apple: The proposed text is not aligned with text in currenet 101-2 spec. Re-l5 spec does not have spherical coverage for downlink CA case. The WF is ongoing. We may need to consider to introduce requirements in a new section .
Intel: The last paragraph looks like requiring both bands in the receiving mode and it also said uplink is configured in one of these band.

Huawei: The proposed concept is only valid for same bands are in the same module. Even for the shared hardware, beam and beam direction could be large for this two bands. Peak EIS achieved for the same AoA in the two bands, case could be different if two bands are supported in different modules.
Verizon: whether the non-located case will be considered as common AoA?
QC: It does not mean UE will not work in non-common AoA cases.
Verizon: 2 AoA was considered in RAN5.

Apple: 2 AoA was considerd only in RRM requirements. 2nd AoA is for neighbour cell measurement. For inter-bands case, simultaneous receiving is considered. For non-colocated deployment scenarios, we need RAN1 design on the multiple panels which is not in Rel-16.
Verizon: Scope of 2AoA is not only for RRM but for RF. RAN1 spec support multiple panels
NTT DoCoMo: In our understanding, RAN1 spec does not preclude the non-colated scenarios.

Apple: In our understanding, multiple panel UE singling is not included in RAN1. Network does not aware if UE support reception in same panel or different panel. We do not preclude the scenarios. Operators shall aware UE may not reach the performance requirements for non-located scenarios.
QC: Not sure how 2 AoA can be used for testing.
Nokia: Only 1 AoA is tested in spec.
MTK: From test perspective, for intra-band EIS test, do we still have go through all the spherical coverage point by point or just go through pointed recordedin the previous single band test.
QC: The requirement is for REFSENS but not for EIS. Simultaneous transmission is not in the scope. The requirements are independent from implementations.
MTK: Whether the common range for peak EIS for these two bands will be considered?
QC: There is no requirements for relative angles for peak EIS. UE will meet the requirements if one of direction can meet peak EIS
Apple: More than one CC per bands has been requested as band combinations. Requirements shall be applied for each CCs
QC: We chose the simple configurations for testing.

interpretation: Final approved documentary outcome, not physical-session-only occurrence or TSG/normative incorporation.
